subject: sandgrouse
title: This Desert Bird Carries Water to Its Chicks in Its Belly Feathers

scenes.text: Its chicks can't fly, and the nearest water is miles away. So Dad delivers.
A male sandgrouse wades into a waterhole and soaks his belly feathers.
They soak up about 25 milliliters, nearly a tenth of a cup.
Then he flies more than 20 kilometers back to the nest.
About half evaporates on the way. The chicks drink the rest straight off his feathers.
Coiled barbs unwind when wet and trap water like a tiny sponge. A flying water bottle.

description:
Male sandgrouse soak their belly feathers at a waterhole and carry water to chicks that can't fly.
He may fly more than 20 kilometers, and the chicks drink straight from his feathers.
What's the strangest way you've seen an animal carry something? Tell us below.
